title: Sitting in and learning from Willie "the Lion" Smith
summary: Carter sat in with Basie and joined Willie the Lion's trio, switching from C melody to alto and learning keys from him.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: Do you remember some of the bands that you played, and that you sat in with?
Well, it was really -- you'd go in a
place where maybe they'd even have just a piano and drums, you know?

I do remember very well that Count Basie was playing at a place where he just played with a drummer. And he was very, very kind to me. I used to go in and sit in with him. I used to go in and sit in with Willie "the Lion" Smith, who also played with just a piano and a drummer.

And then one of the jobs that I had in the earliest, was with Willie "the Lion" Smith when he added me to his duo to make a trio. Piano, drums and saxophone. And I must say, I certainly learned a lot from him.

What happened was, I was playing a C Melody saxophone, which I had bought, and I bought this because that was what I understood Frankie Trumbauer played, and then Willie told me -- Willie "The Lion," that is, said if I was going to play with orchestras, I'd have to have an Alto or a Tenor, because they weren't using C Melodies; you know -- there wasn't any music being written for them in the orchestral parts -- and he was quite right, at that time.

So I got an Alto saxophone, and I'll tell you a very funny thing he used to do to me, which wasn't funny, really; it was very good for me -- but in playing the C Melody saxophone, you are also always playing in the concert key, just

as the piano -- he's playing an E flat, and you're playing an E flat; he's playing in C and you're playing in C. But when I got the Alto, well, I started playing in keys or having to play in keys with which I was not familiar. The only sharp key I played in before was the one sharp which was G, but playing with Willie The Lion Smith, when he was in G, I was in four sharps, E, when he was in C, I was in 3 sharps, A, which was extremely difficult for me.

So I would adjust the mouthpiece to change the key, you know -- pull the mouthpiece out, to change the key to make it an easier key - and he used to see me doing this, and he'd give me the dickens about it and make me, you know, play in the keys I was supposed to be in, you know, he'd say, "C'mon, kid, put that mouthpiece where it should be -- push it back in". He knew, you know, every trick that I was pulling.

And then after I finally had gotten a little better control of the keys, he would just play in any key -- you never knew what he was gonna do; he caught himself sometimes trying to trick you, you know, just for fun --and it was a very valuable musical experience for me, playing with him.
